application.cover_letter_markdown:
After sixteen years building signal processing capability at Sinikaari Optics, I am looking for a position where I can apply the full scope of what I have learned. The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara is that position.

My career at Sinikaari has taken me from pure algorithm development into the kind of hands-on system work that requires you to think across multiple engineering layers simultaneously. I started writing spectral analysis code for optical inspection and over the years expanded into embedded DSP implementation in C and C++, where I learned what it means to get algorithms running under real-time constraints on actual hardware rather than in simulation. I have also developed significant production Python capability – automated testing frameworks, batch processing pipelines, deployment scripts – which has become an increasingly large part of my daily work.

What I think distinguishes my profile is that these are not isolated competencies. I work across all of them in my day-to-day role, and I understand how they connect in a real engineering workflow. Too many engineers are specialists in one layer – they can design an algorithm but cannot debug a hardware integration, or they can write production code but have never characterised a signal chain end to end. I do all of it, routinely.

On the measurement side, I have built up practical experience in RF measurement and characterisation through years of working with real hardware and real signal chains. This is not something you acquire from textbooks. It comes from thousands of hours on a bench figuring out why the measured performance refuses to match the simulation.

My academic grounding is strong. The training I received has served me well throughout my career and I continue to build on it. I have also maintained a presence in the research community through technical publications and conference contributions, which keeps my thinking sharp and helps me evaluate new methods critically rather than just adopting whatever is fashionable.

There is a gap on my CV from October 2010 to late 2011 when I was recovering from a serious illness. I came back to Sinikaari and picked up where I left off. If anything, the experience gave me a clearer sense of what I want from a working environment and what kind of problems I want to spend my time solving.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara specifically is the level of technical difficulty your instrument work operates at. I have spent time working in the Oulu area on deployment projects and found the engineering environment there to be focused and serious in a way that suits me. The problems you solve demand someone who can move between theory and practice without losing rigour in either direction, and that is how I have built my career.

I look forward to discussing this further.

Camille Fischer

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Dear Kaikuvaara Oy Recruitment,

Oulu's position as a Nordic hub for RF and photonics engineering is something I have followed with professional interest for a long time. The density of serious technical talent in the region, and Kaikuvaara's role within that cluster, is a large part of why I am writing.

I am a signal processing engineer with more than 25 years of continuous experience, most of it at Boreal Photonics where I have worked since 1999. My technical profile covers embedded DSP development in C and C++, production Python for automated testing and data processing workflows, RF measurement and characterisation, and advanced estimation techniques including Kalman filtering and state estimation. These have been part of my daily engineering practice for decades, not peripheral additions.

My background at CRIT provided a solid academic base, and I view that foundation as applicable to the kind of precision engineering work that Kaikuvaara undertakes. The theoretical grounding is not an add-on – it shapes how I approach every engineering problem.

I was made redundant from a prior position in 2001 and spent approximately a year requalifying before establishing myself at Boreal Photonics, where I have been since. That transition, while difficult at the time, ultimately redirected me toward the photonic sensing domain where I have spent the most productive phase of my career.

Throughout my time at Boreal Photonics, I have valued working in a technically rigorous environment where precision matters and shortcuts are not tolerated. That standard is something I would expect to find – and would want to find – at Kaikuvaara.

I should note that while my primary domain has been optical sensing, the underlying signal processing methodology is transferable. The mathematics of spectral decomposition and multi-channel analysis does not care what kind of sensor generated the data, and I have always worked at the algorithmic level where that generality holds.

Kaikuvaara's engineering challenges and the broader Oulu technical ecosystem are both factors in my interest. I believe there is a strong alignment between what you need and what I offer, and I would welcome the opportunity to explore that further.

Kind regards,
Marika Heinonen

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Your posting for a Senior Signal Processing Engineer immediately resonated with me. Kaikuvaara's work on spaceborne and airborne instruments represents the kind of mission-critical engineering I have always wanted to be part of, and I believe I bring the right combination of skills and experience to contribute to your team.

I have over a decade of experience in signal processing at Fenno Radar Technologies. During that time I have developed comprehensive expertise across multiple areas directly relevant to what you are looking for. My phased-array and beamforming signal processing skills are well established, as is my experience with embedded DSP development in C and C++. I am proficient in production Python for algorithm deployment and pipeline automation. I have hands-on RF measurement and characterisation experience and strong grounding in Kalman filtering and state estimation theory.

Beyond the core signal processing work, I bring direct experience with the constraints and requirements of satellite and airborne platforms. I understand what it means to design processing chains that must perform reliably in environments where you cannot simply reboot the system or swap a board. Thermal variation, power budgets, vibration – these are not abstract concerns for me.

I have also taken on team leadership responsibilities at various points in my career, coordinating technical workstreams and mentoring more junior engineers. This is something I value and consider a core part of what a senior engineer should contribute.

What makes me effective as a senior engineer is that I do not just do one of these things. I work across the full stack – algorithm design, embedded implementation, Python tooling, measurement, estimation. When you have worked across all of these areas for long enough, you start to see the connections between them that specialists miss, and that is where the real value of a senior hire comes in.

My education at CRIT gave me a strong theoretical foundation that has underpinned everything I have built professionally since. I consider my academic background highly relevant to this role, and I have continued to invest in that theoretical base through my work.

I have followed Kaikuvaara for some time and the company's focus on pushing the boundaries of remote-sensing instrumentation is genuinely exciting to me. The engineering challenges involved in building instruments that operate on satellite and airborne platforms – constrained processing, reliability under harsh conditions, precision measurement in demanding environments – are precisely the problems I want to be solving.

I would be very happy to discuss my background in more detail.

Best regards,
Aleksi Korhonen

application.cover_letter_markdown:
The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara is exactly the kind of position I have been looking for – one where the technical depth is real and the stakes of the work are not abstract. After 25 years at Boreal Photonics I am not looking for a change out of restlessness; I am looking for a context where the scope of problems matches what I can actually deliver.

My career at Boreal has been in photonic sensor systems, which is a domain that shares more with Kaikuvaara's work than it might appear on the surface. The core signal processing challenges – detection at low SNR, signal recovery in noisy and non-stationary environments, algorithm-hardware co-design – are fundamentally the same whether the sensor is optical or RF. What changes is the physics at the front end; the engineering behind it translates.

I bring strong capabilities in embedded DSP development in C and C++, which I consider essential for any engineer working on real-time instrument systems. My production Python skills have also become a central part of how I work, from simulation frameworks to automated acceptance testing to deployment tooling. And I have extensive RF measurement and characterisation experience that gives me the practical instinct for what a signal chain actually does versus what it should do on paper. I consider the ability to move across these layers – implementation, measurement, simulation – to be what defines a senior signal processing engineer.

What I find genuinely exciting about Kaikuvaara is the remote-sensing instrumentation work – the idea of building systems that have to function autonomously on spaceborne and airborne platforms, where the engineering decisions you make during development determine whether the mission succeeds or fails. That combination of precision, reliability, and the physical reality of harsh operating environments is something I have always been drawn to.

On a practical note, I have been actively considering a move to Oulu for some time. My partner has family connections in the region and we have visited regularly over the past several years. Relocation is not a hypothetical for us – it is something we are already planning, and this role would give it a professional anchor that makes the timing right.

I have spent a quarter of a century building technical depth in a single company, which I know can read as narrow. But I see it differently: I have had the continuity to develop real expertise rather than skimming across roles, and I think Kaikuvaara's problems are complex enough to benefit from someone who has that kind of depth. I am not chasing a title. I want to work on hard problems with people who care about getting them right.

Rasmus Bianchi

In my first year at Hohtola Photonics I have been responsible for coordinating the documentation and validation workflows for two product release cycles, and that experience has confirmed that I work best in engineering environments where precision and deadlines both matter.

I studied management engineering in Milan and came back to Finland wanting to work in a technical industry where the products are complex and the engineering standards are high. These are not glamorous tasks but they are the kind of work that, done badly, creates genuine delays and confusion downstream.

What attracts me to the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara is the chance to work in a company whose instruments operate at the edge of what current technology can do. The combination of radar engineering and precision instrumentation in your Senior Signal Processing Engineer posting is what made me look more closely at Kaikuvaara. I have been following the growth of Oulu's RF and photonics engineering cluster for some time, partly because I spent eight months on secondment there through Fenno Radar and got a direct look at the technical community.

My background is in multi-channel radar signal processing. At Fenno Radar I work on beamforming algorithm design, embedded DSP firmware development, and RF front-end characterisation – essentially the full chain from antenna to processed output. I also built the automated Python test framework that our team uses for nightly regression testing and release qualification. The technical work is demanding and the team is strong, but Kaikuvaara's focus on precision instrumentation represents a different class of problem that I think would push me in directions I want to go.

I should mention that I am a Finnish citizen, so there are no work authorisation requirements to consider.

What specifically draws me to Kaikuvaara's engineering is the integration challenge that precision instruments present. Radar systems and measurement instruments share the same core constraint: the signal processing must perform within the boundaries imposed by the hardware, the operating environment, and the underlying physics. Getting that right, end to end, is what I find most satisfying about this kind of work, and it is why I have stayed in the domain rather than moving into higher-paying software roles where the constraints are looser.

I grew up in the Pirkanmaa region and my family is still in the Tampere area, though I have no strong ties keeping me there specifically. I spent a substantial part of 2022 working out of the Fenno Radar Oulu facility and genuinely liked the city – the scale of the engineering community, the fact that people know each other across companies, the general pace of things. I think that kind of environment matters when you are building something that has to be right.

I would be glad to discuss this further and learn more about the challenges your team is working on.

Outi Virtanen

Personal / Side Projects

4-Element ULA Beamforming Demonstrator (2022–2023)
Built a four-element uniform linear array beamformer as a personal project to get hands-on experience with phased-array principles. Hardware: four RTL-SDR dongles synchronised via a common 28.8 MHz reference clock, half-wavelength-spaced dipoles on a hand-etched PCB at 433 MHz. Software: Python-based acquisition using pyrtlsdr, with Capon beamforming for direction-of-arrival estimation. The system resolves two narrowband sources separated by approximately 25 degrees at 15 dB SNR. A weekend project that took about seven months of weekends to get working properly – no publication, no employer involvement.

MSc Thesis: Adaptive Interference Cancellation in Wideband Receivers (2013)
Designed and evaluated a multichannel adaptive filtering architecture for suppression of co-site interference in wideband RF receivers. Combined LMS-family algorithms with constrained optimisation to maintain receiver sensitivity in the presence of strong adjacent-band emitters.

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Kaikuvaara's work on mission-critical remote-sensing instruments is the reason I am applying for this role rather than staying where I am comfortable. At Polaris RF Labs I have a stable position doing work I find interesting, but the prospect of contributing to instruments that operate on spaceborne and airborne platforms – where the engineering decisions made during development directly determine mission success – is something I have wanted to pursue for a long time.

My professional background is in RF receiver systems. For the past twelve years at Polaris I have worked on wideband receiver products, doing everything from RF characterisation on the bench to tracking loop algorithm design. One area where I have built particular depth is embedded DSP. A significant part of my work involves writing and optimising real-time signal processing code in C and C++ for TI DSP and ARM Cortex-M platforms – carrier acquisition loops, synchronisation engines, real-time spectral monitoring modules. These are not simulations running on a workstation; they run on hardware with fixed clock budgets and you find out quickly whether your approach actually holds up.

On the software tooling side, I have built and maintained several production Python tools that our engineering team relies on daily – automated test execution and reporting, measurement instrument control libraries, and a build verification framework that runs against our firmware every night. These are not throwaway scripts; they are versioned, tested, documented, and other engineers depend on them. Building that kind of infrastructure is not the most visible part of the job but I believe it is one of the most impactful. When your test tooling is solid, the whole team catches regressions earlier, which matters enormously in a product cycle where late-found bugs are expensive.

I should note that Polaris RF Labs is an English-speaking workplace. Our team includes engineers from Finland, Hungary, Germany, India, and the UK, and all technical communication – design reviews, documentation, daily coordination, everything – happens in English. I have worked in this environment for my entire career and it is completely natural.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara specifically is the integration challenge that mission-critical instruments present. In my experience, the hardest engineering problems sit at the interfaces: between algorithm and hardware, between simulation and measurement, between what the spec promises and what the physics delivers. Instruments that operate on remote platforms add another dimension – they must work without intervention, in harsh environments, under constrained resources. I find that combination deeply motivating.

I am based in Helsinki but have already been looking at Oulu as a place to move, for both professional and personal reasons. I would welcome the chance to discuss this role with you.

Matteo Horvath
